reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Computation of statutory and court time periods
headings.reviewNote: Excludes first day, includes last day unless Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, and excludes intermediate weekend days and holidays when period is less than seven days.

headings.title: Discretionary time enlargement and nonextendable deadlines
headings.reviewNote: Permits court to enlarge time periods upon application or for excusable neglect, but prohibits enlargement for commencing actions, taking appeals, or motions for new trial.

headings.title: Court term expiration effect on pending actions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the expiration of a court term does not affect or limit time periods or the court's authority over pending civil actions.

headings.title: Motion service deadlines and supporting affidavits
headings.reviewNote: Requires service of written motions and notice at least five days before hearing and sets timing for service of supporting and opposing affidavits.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections and Bowling v. Webb Gas (505 S.W.2d 39) annotation on time computation, discretionary enlargement limits, term expiration, and motion service.

headings.title: Service of pleadings and papers subsequent to original petition
headings.reviewNote: Mandates service of subsequent pleadings and motions on all affected parties, exempting parties in default unless new or additional claims are asserted.

headings.title: Methods of service on attorney of record or party
headings.reviewNote: Requires service on the attorney of record unless personal service is ordered, specifying delivery methods at office or usual place of abode.

headings.title: Service orders in multidefendant actions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court in actions with unusually large numbers of defendants to dispense with service of pleadings between defendants and deem crossclaims denied.

headings.title: Filing deadline for served papers
headings.reviewNote: Requires papers subsequent to the petition to be filed with the court either before service or within five days thereafter.

headings.title: Filing with court clerk or presiding judge
headings.reviewNote: Directs filing of pleadings and papers with the court clerk, permitting filing directly with a judge who notes the filing date and transmits them to the clerk.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections governing service of subsequent pleadings and motions, service methods, multidefendant orders, five-day filing, and filing with clerk or judge.

headings.title: Methods of instituting suits in courts of record
headings.reviewNote: Outlines methods of commencing actions in courts of record by filing a petition with voluntary appearance or issuance of a summons or writ of attachment.

headings.title: Statutory definition of suit commencement
headings.reviewNote: Defines commencement of suit as filing petition or statement and suing out process; source note observes subsection 2 is superseded by Supreme Court Rule 53.01.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections and Keys v. Nigro (913 S.W.2d 947) annotation noting subsection 2 is overruled by Supreme Court Rule 53.01.

headings.title: Authorized persons for service of process
headings.reviewNote: Designates sheriffs, deputies, coroners upon disqualification, or court-appointed special process servers to execute service of process.

headings.title: Taxation of special process server fees as costs
headings.reviewNote: Permits a party to apply for fees paid to a special process server to be awarded in judgment, authorizing the court to enter judgment in a reasonable amount.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections and coroner cross-references (58.190, 58.200); removed extratextual sheriff-rate cap from subsection 2 note.

headings.title: Methods of personal service of summons and petition
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes procedures for personal service of summons and petition upon individuals, incapacitated persons, corporations, partnerships, and public entities.

headings.title: Written acknowledgment and waiver of service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes defendant to acknowledge service in writing on the writ, waiving formal service by an officer.

headings.title: Service upon defendant refusal to receive process
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an officer's offer to read process and statement of its nature constitutes valid service if the defendant refuses receipt.

headings.title: Service by mail and cost shifting for nonacknowledgment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes service of summons and petition by first class mail with statutory acknowledgment forms, taxing costs of subsequent service if acknowledgment is withheld.

headings.title: Statutory form for notice and acknowledgment by mail
headings.reviewNote: Sets forth the mandatory statutory form for notice and acknowledgment of service of summons and petition by mail.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections, embedded mail-acknowledgment form, and Ward/Kirlin annotations on personal service, refusal, written waiver, and first-class mail service.

headings.title: Actions eligible for service by mail or publication
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes service by mail or publication in actions in rem, quasi in rem, property, probate, trust, marital status, or adoption proceedings.

headings.title: Application and clerk procedure for service by mail
headings.reviewNote: Requires verified petition or affidavit establishing grounds for service by registered mail with delivery receipt requested.

headings.title: Grounds and order of court for service by publication
headings.reviewNote: Details verified allegations required to obtain a court order of publication in an authorized newspaper when personal or mail service cannot be had.

headings.title: Service by publication against unknown defendants
headings.reviewNote: Regulates allegations and published notice requirements when defendant names or heirs are unknown to the plaintiff.

headings.title: Discretionary personal service alongside mail or publication notice
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court, when ordering notice by mail or newspaper publication, to also issue a summons for personal service in the ordinary manner if obtainable.

headings.title: Personal service outside state in lieu of publication
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes personal delivery of summons and petition out of state in lieu of service by mail or publication, requiring return affidavit.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections and Union Shoe (441 S.W.2d 321) annotation; corrected subsection 5 title to remove erroneous "outside state" limitation.

headings.title: Officer written return of process
headings.reviewNote: Requires every officer receiving a writ of process for service to make a signed written return stating time, place, and manner of service.

headings.title: Affidavit of service by appointed process server
headings.reviewNote: Requires non-officer process servers to file an affidavit certifying the time, place, and manner of process execution.

headings.title: Proof of service by registered mail
headings.reviewNote: Requires proof of mail service by clerk mailing certificate and the return registered mail receipt under section 506.160(2).

headings.title: Proof of service by publication in newspaper
headings.reviewNote: Requires proof of publication by affidavit stating publication dates and newspaper with attached notice copy, plus clerk mailing certificate where address was stated.

headings.title: Prohibition of civil arrest or imprisonment on mesne process
headings.reviewNote: Explicitly bars arrest, bail, or imprisonment on any mesne process or execution arising from any civil action.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections; tightened subsection 3 title to "registered mail" and corrected extratextual details in subsections 1, 3, and 4 notes.

headings.title: Definition of person under nonresident motorist law
headings.reviewNote: Defines "person" under section 506.210 to include motor vehicle or trailer owners, operating agents, and persons in charge with express or implied owner consent.

headings.title: Definition of restricted registered mail
headings.reviewNote: Defines restricted, registered mail as mail requiring delivery only to the addressee with conspicuous endorsement.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections defining "person" (removed extratextual "personal representatives" from note) and "restricted, registered mail".

headings.title: Service on secretary of state as nonresident agent
headings.reviewNote: Directs service of process on nonresident motorists by delivering summons and petition copies to the secretary of state (or chief clerk in absence) at office.

headings.title: Secretary of state notice and transmittal to defendant
headings.reviewNote: Directs the secretary of state to immediately mail notice and copies of process to nonresident defendants by restricted, registered mail.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on secretary of state service (removed extratextual fee reference from subsection 1 note) and restricted registered mail notice.

headings.title: Venue for actions against nonresident motorists
headings.reviewNote: Governs venue for nonresident motorist suits under sections 506.200 to 506.320 (*506.320 repealed in 1996), including actions with resident codefendants.

headings.title: Venue for civil identity theft actions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes filing civil identity theft suits under section 570.223 where the offense or any element occurred, where defendant or victim resides, or where property was located.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections and repealed section 506.320 footnote; aligned subsection 2 note to property-location venue.

headings.title: Assessment of partial court costs against indigent offenders
headings.reviewNote: Mandates assessment of partial court costs equal to twenty percent of the greater of six-month average deposits or balance for indigent inmates.

headings.title: Duration of partial cost assessment order
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the trial court's partial payment order remains effective through final judgment in trial or appellate courts.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on 20-percent partial court cost assessment for indigent offenders and duration through final trial or appellate judgment.

headings.title: Predocketing judicial screening of offender civil complaints
headings.reviewNote: Directs courts to screen offender complaints against public entities or employees and dismiss frivolous, malicious, or immune claims.

headings.title: Attorney fees and costs on dismissal of frivolous claims
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to award attorney fees and court costs to defendants when an offender's civil action or appeal is dismissed as frivolous.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on judicial screening of offender civil complaints against governmental entities/employees and discretionary fee/cost awards on dismissal.

headings.title: Mandatory administrative exhaustion for offender civil suits
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits offender civil actions prior to exhausting administrative remedies, subject to an exception for constitutional deprivations.

headings.title: Dismissal of defective claims prior to administrative exhaustion
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes immediate dismissal of facially frivolous, malicious, non-cognizable, or immune claims without awaiting administrative exhaustion.

headings.title: Federal statutory limitations on state court remedies
headings.reviewNote: Subjects state court civil actions by offenders asserting federal law claims to all remedial limitations established under federal law.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections on mandatory offender administrative exhaustion (except constitutional deprivations), pre-exhaustion dismissal, and federal remedy limits.

headings.title: Long-arm jurisdiction for acts committed within state
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates transactions and acts within Missouri that submit nonresident individuals and corporations to personal jurisdiction.

headings.title: Matrimonial and domestic relations long-arm jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Establishes personal jurisdiction over former marital residents in actions for dissolution, legal separation, maintenance, and child support.

headings.title: Restriction to claims arising from enumerated long-arm acts
headings.reviewNote: Restricts long-arm personal jurisdiction strictly to causes of action arising from the specific acts enumerated in the statute.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections and extensive long-arm personal jurisdiction annotations covering enumerated acts, marital residence, and claim-arising restriction.

headings.title: Personal out-of-state service on individuals and corporations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes personal service outside Missouri on nonresident individuals and corporate officers or registered agents with full in-state legal effect.

headings.title: Transmittal of process and fees to out-of-state officer
headings.reviewNote: Directs sending process, petition copies, and required fees to an authorized court or officer at the out-of-state location of the defendant.

headings.title: Return affidavit of out-of-state process server
headings.reviewNote: Requires return of an out-of-state process server affidavit specifying time, place, and manner of service to prove valid execution.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections governing personal out-of-state service on individuals and corporations, transmittal to out-of-state officers, and return affidavits.

headings.title: Personal judgment power upon long-arm service
headings.reviewNote: Confers court authority to render personal judgments against nonresident individuals and entities served under long-arm provisions.

headings.title: Waiting period and standard for setting aside default judgment
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits default judgments within thirty days of long-arm service and governs standards for setting aside judgments.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on personal judgment authority upon long-arm service, 30-day default waiting period, and standard to set aside defaults.

headings.title: Short title of No Foreign Laws Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates the statutory section as the No Foreign Laws Act.

headings.title: Definitions of foreign law and fundamental rights
headings.reviewNote: Defines foreign law and fundamental constitutional rights guaranteed by state and federal constitutions.

headings.title: Invalidation of rulings and contracts applying foreign law
headings.reviewNote: Declares void and unenforceable administrative, arbitral, or judicial rulings and contractual choices of law denying fundamental rights.

headings.title: Judicial nonenforcement of judgments violating fundamental rights
headings.reviewNote: Bars courts from enforcing foreign judgments, contracts, or family law decrees inconsistent with constitutional fundamental rights or public policy.

headings.title: Statutory exemptions, ecclesiastical matters, and federal preemption
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not affect supreme court precedent, religious doctrine or clergy governance, corporate entities, or federal preemption.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of the No Foreign Laws Act covering definitions, void rulings/contracts, nonenforcement, and precedent/ecclesiastical/corporate/federal exemptions.
